name: Beriah
overview: Beriah was a male descendant of Shimei from the tribe of Levi, as recorded in 1 Chronicles 23:10. His identity is primarily noted through his lineage, linking him to the Levitical family. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide additional personal details or notable events concerning him.
namesAndTitles: The name Beriah means 'prominent' or 'excellent' in Hebrew, reflecting a proper name given in the biblical text. There is no indication that this name was divinely given, but it carries connotations of distinction within the Levitical line as noted in 1 Chronicles 23:10.
familyAndRelationships: Beriah is explicitly identified as a descendant of Shimei, establishing a clear familial connection within the tribe of Levi. Scripture does not record other family relationships beyond this lineage.
scriptureSignificance: Beriah's significance lies in his role as a member of the Levitical lineage, specifically as a descendant of Shimei. This connection situates him within the priestly tribe entrusted with religious duties in Israel, emphasizing the continuity of Levitical service. Although not prominent in narrative events, his mention underscores the detailed genealogical records that affirm God's providential preservation of His chosen priestly family.
